questions.section: PART THREE: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 Marks) - Question 1
questions.question:
1.
   A) What is photograph? (1 mark)

   B) Distinguish between Ground photograph and Aerial photograph. (2 marks)

   C) State any three uses of Gradient. (3 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
A) A photograph is a picture of an object or part of the earth's surface taken with a camera.

B)
   - Ground (terrestrial) photograph: taken from the ground with the camera held by a person standing on the ground, so it shows a side view of features.
   - Aerial photograph: taken from the air (aircraft, drone or satellite) with the camera pointing down, so it shows a view from above of a large area.

C) Any three uses of gradient:
   1. Helps in deciding suitable land for farming, settlement and building
   2. Helps in planning and constructing roads, railways and drainage
   3. Shows how steep a slope is, to estimate the risk of soil erosion and the speed of water flow (also useful for siting dams / hydroelectric power and for hikers)

questions.section: PART THREE: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 Marks) - Question 2
questions.question:
2.
   A) Define the term agriculture (1 mark)

   B) Mention any three among reasons facilitated agricultural beginning in middle east. (3 marks)

   C) Differentiate between intensive and extensive farming (4 marks)
      | Intensive Farming | Extensive farming |
      | ................. | ................. |
      | ................. | ................. |
      | ................. | ................. |

matching_pairs.item: Intensive farming: small farms (small land area)
matching_pairs.match: Extensive farming: large farms (large land area)

matching_pairs.item: Intensive farming: high labour and capital input per hectare
matching_pairs.match: Extensive farming: low labour and capital input per hectare

matching_pairs.item: Intensive farming: high yield per hectare
matching_pairs.match: Extensive farming: low yield per hectare

questions.answer_guide:
A) Agriculture is the science and art of cultivating crops and rearing animals for food and other products.

B) Any three:
   1. Fertile soils in the river valleys (Tigris, Euphrates and Nile)
   2. Availability of water from rivers for irrigation
   3. Favourable climate with mild winters, and wild plants (wheat, barley) and animals (sheep, goats) that were easy to domesticate

C) See the table pairs: intensive farming = small land, high inputs per hectare, high yields per hectare; extensive farming = large land, low inputs per hectare, low yields per hectare.

questions.section: PART THREE: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 Marks) - Question 3
questions.question:
3.
   A) Differentiate between mining and mineral.
      i. Mining: (1 mark)
      ii. Minerals: (1 mark)

   B) State the three methods of mining minerals. (3 marks)

   C) Describe any Three problems faced mining minerals from earth. (3 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
A)
   i. Mining: the process of extracting (digging out) minerals from the earth's crust.
   ii. Minerals: naturally occurring inorganic substances with a definite chemical composition found in rocks of the earth's crust.

B)
   1. Opencast (surface) mining
   2. Underground (shaft) mining
   3. Quarrying (alluvial / placer mining or drilling are also accepted)

C) Any three:
   1. Lack of capital and modern technology, so mining is slow and costly
   2. Poor transport and infrastructure to carry the minerals to markets
   3. Accidents (collapsing tunnels), health hazards and environmental damage such as land destruction and pollution (also shortage of skilled labour and insecurity)

questions.question:
4.
   A) Define the term transportation. (1 mark)

   B) Name the type of land transport represented by the diagram. (1 mark)

   C) List any two dis-advantages of the above type of transport. (2 marks)

   D) Distinguish between air and water transportation. (2 marks)

diagram.caption: A camel carrying a large load on its back (the paper shows a photograph of a loaded camel).

questions.answer_guide:
A) Transportation is the movement of people, goods and services from one place to another.

B) Animal transport (the camel, a pack animal).

C) Any two disadvantages:
   1. It is slow
   2. It carries only small loads and cannot cover long distances (animals get tired, sick or die in drought)

D)
   - Air transport uses aircraft in the air: it is the fastest but the most expensive, and is used for passengers and valuable or perishable goods.
   - Water transport uses ships, boats or dhows on seas, rivers and lakes: it is slower but cheaper, and is used for heavy and bulky goods.

questions.section: PART THREE: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 Marks) - Question 5
questions.question:
5.
   A) Define the term Energy. (1 mark)

   B) List any three difference between renewable and non-renewable energy? (3 Marks)
      | Renewable energy | Non-renewable |
      | 1. ............... | 1. ............... |
      | 2. ............... | 2. ............... |
      | 3. ............... | 3. ............... |

   C) Describe any two causes of the Energy crisis in the world. (2 marks)

matching_pairs.item: Renewable: can be replaced naturally and does not run out (e.g. solar, wind, geothermal)
matching_pairs.match: Non-renewable: finite, cannot be replaced once used (e.g. coal, petroleum, natural gas)

matching_pairs.item: Renewable: clean, causes little or no pollution
matching_pairs.match: Non-renewable: pollutes the environment (smoke, carbon dioxide)

matching_pairs.item: Renewable: usually has a high set-up cost but low running cost
matching_pairs.match: Non-renewable: cheaper to start with but the cost rises as the supply declines

questions.answer_guide:
A) Energy is the capacity (ability) to do work.

B) See the table pairs.

C) Any two:
   1. Rapid population growth and industrialization increase the demand for energy
   2. Depletion of fossil fuels (oil, coal) and over-dependence on them
   (also: high prices, wars and political conflicts, wastage of energy, lack of investment in renewable energy)

questions.section: PART THREE: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 Marks) - Question 6
questions.question:
6.
   A) Define the term fishery. (1 mark)

   B) State four main types of fishes. (4 Marks)

   C) Mention any two among traditional methods of fishing. (2 marks)

   D) Identify two possible solutions for the problems faced fishing in Somalia. (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
A) A fishery is an area (or industry) where fish and other water animals are caught, processed and sold.

B) Four main types of fish:
   1. Pelagic fish (live near the surface, e.g. tuna, sardines)
   2. Demersal fish (live near the sea bottom, e.g. cod)
   3. Crustaceans (e.g. lobsters, shrimps)
   4. Molluscs (e.g. oysters, squid)
   (freshwater fish are also accepted)

C) Any two:
   1. Hooks and lines
   2. Hand nets, traps / baskets, spears or harpoons

D) Any two:
   1. Stop illegal foreign fishing and patrol the coast / improve security against piracy
   2. Provide modern boats, equipment, cold storage and training to local fishermen

questions.section: PART THREE: STRUCTURED QUESTIONS (65 Marks) - Question 8
questions.question:
8.
   A) Define term forest. (1 Mark)

   B) Briefly explain how the following factors can influence Forests.
      I. Temperature (1 Mark)
      II. Rainfall (1 Mark)

   C) List any three importance of forests. (3 marks)
questions.answer_guide:
A) A forest is a large area of land covered with trees and other vegetation growing close together.

B)
   I. Temperature: trees grow best where it is warm to moderate; high temperatures with moisture produce dense tropical forests, while very low temperatures limit tree growth (only hardy coniferous forests survive).
   II. Rainfall: heavy, well-distributed rainfall supports dense evergreen forests, whereas little rainfall produces sparse trees and grassland or desert.

C) Any three:
   1. Source of timber, firewood and charcoal
   2. Help rainfall formation and regulate climate; absorb carbon dioxide
   3. Prevent soil erosion; habitat for wildlife; tourism and source of medicine, food and income

B) Any two objectives:

   B) Look at the below diagram and then answer the following questions.

      ii. List any three growing conditions of the above cereal (3 marks)

questions.answer_guide:
A) Cereals are crops of the grass family that are grown for their edible grains (e.g. wheat, maize, rice, sorghum).

B)
   i. Maize (corn)
   ii. Any three growing conditions:
      1. Warm temperatures (about 18 °C to 27 °C)
      2. Moderate rainfall (about 500 mm to 1200 mm)
      3. Fertile, well-drained loamy soils with plenty of sunshine

questions.section: PART FOUR: EXTENDED QUESTIONS (15 MARKS) - Answer ONLY THREE among the following questions - Question 4
questions.question:
4.
   A) Define the term industrialization. (1 Mark)

   B) List two types of secondary industries. (2 Marks)

   C) Count down any two significances of industries. (2 Marks)
questions.answer_guide:
A) Industrialization is the process of developing industries in a country, changing its economy from mainly farming to manufacturing and processing goods.

B) Any two:
   1. Manufacturing industries (e.g. textiles, furniture)
   2. Processing industries (e.g. food processing, fish canning) (construction is also a secondary industry)

C) Any two:
   1. Creates employment and raises incomes and living standards
   2. Adds value to raw materials and earns foreign exchange (also promotes development of infrastructure and towns)
